description: A sixteen bit shift register sequencer after Music Thing Modular's Turing Machine, giving a stepped voltage, a gate from the register's top bit and a random bit stream

params.text: Sets how likely the bit coming round is replaced by a fresh random one; with the write switch off and Write Mode set to Standard the register repeats unchanged and this knob changes nothing
Sets how many of the register's top bits are read into the stepped output, 1 to 16; the loop itself is sixteen steps long whatever this is set to
Sets which way a newly written bit falls, fully anticlockwise always low, fully clockwise always high and even odds at the centre
Allows fresh random bits to be written into the register; switched off, the pattern comes round unchanged
Fills the register with a fresh random sixteen bit pattern and stores it as the pattern the reset input returns to

inputs.text: Shifts the register one place on each rising edge above 1V
Reloads the stored seed pattern on a rising edge above 1V, without shifting the register
Nothing in the module acts on this jack: its voltage is added to the change probability only after that probability has already been used, and the sum is then thrown away
Adds to the number of top bits read into the stepped output, 1.6 bits per volt, and the total is held between 1 and 16
Adds to the bias of a newly written bit, 10V covering the whole of the bias knob, and the total is held between always low and always high

outputs.text: The register's top bits read as a number and scaled between 0V and the top of the range set on the menu, which is 5V unless you change it
10V while the register's top bit is high, or a 50ms pulse each time that bit changes when Pulse Mode is set to Tap
A fresh random choice of 0V or 10V drawn every sample, taken from neither the register nor the clock

notes: both expanders go to the right: a Gates expander only works as the immediate right neighbour, while Flow expanders work anywhere down the chain of modules to the right
the register is filled with a random pattern when the module is added, so a clock alone is enough to get a sequence out of it
menu: Mode: Normal, Poly Ryhtmic — Normal shifts the register once per clock; Poly Ryhtmic shifts it only on some clocks and writes no new bits at all, so the pattern is fixed
Pitch Output Range: 5V, 3V, 1V — sets the top of the stepped output's range
Write Mode: Standard, Evolving — Standard writes new bits only while the write switch is on; Evolving always writes them, at a tenth of the change knob's probability
Pulse Mode: Gate, Tap — Gate holds the pulse output high for as long as the register's top bit is high; Tap gives a 50ms pulse each time that bit changes

inputs.0:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.1:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.2:
one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V, and read to no effect.
inputs.3:
0 to 10V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V, so the knob alone; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
inputs.4:
±5V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V, leaving the knob alone; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
